sections.content: You know the subjunctive after value judgments such as *es importante que* from A2 Unit 27, and *el hecho de que* from B2 Unit 6. At C1 the judgments get stronger and the register more formal: *Resulta inadmisible que…*, *Es de lamentar que…*, *Es deplorable que…*. The fact is real and both writer and reader know it. The writer only judges it, so the verb after *que* is in the subjunctive. After a past fact use the perfect subjunctive (B1 Unit 37): *Es de lamentar que no se haya consultado a los vecinos*. A phrase that says something is *true* works differently: *Resulta evidente que* + indicative.

sections.title: Judgment and evidence
rows: Resulta inadmisible que el ayuntamiento aplace la decisión.
It is unacceptable that the council puts off the decision. (judgment: subjunctive)
Es de lamentar que no se haya consultado a los vecinos.
It is regrettable that the residents were not consulted. (judgment of a past fact: perfect subjunctive)
El hecho de que los comerciantes protesten es comprensible.
The fact that the shopkeepers protest is understandable. (the fact first, the comment after)
Resulta evidente que el centro necesita cambios.
It is obvious that the centre needs changes. (evidence: indicative)

items.spanish: Es deplorable que nadie haya respondido a los vecinos.
items.english: It is deplorable that nobody has answered the residents.

items.spanish: Resulta preocupante que el plan no tenga fecha.
items.english: It is worrying that the plan has no date.

items.spanish: Es encomiable que el ayuntamiento haya abierto el debate.
items.english: It is praiseworthy that the council has opened the debate.

items.spanish: Resultaba injustificable que se esperara tanto.
items.english: It was unjustifiable that people waited so long.

sections.content: English says "It is unacceptable that the council *delays*", with the plain present. Spanish does not: the judgment itself calls for the subjunctive, so *aplace*. But a phrase that only points to the truth (*Resulta evidente que*) takes the indicative. Ask yourself: am I judging the fact, or saying it is true? And write *el hecho de que*, with *de*: *el hecho que* is a slip that careful writing avoids.
